Virtue Effect: You learn quickly from battle, gaining increased experience.
Sin Effect: Temptation dulls your caution, reducing your resistance to debilitating effects.
Description: Humans are something you can relate to. They are the most versatile of all races, making a viable option for all classes. While they have no magical resistances, they also have no weaknesses.

Virtue Effect: You see through deception, suffering fewer penalties when fighting the unseen or obscured.
Sin Effect: Your pride resists aid, slightly reducing healing received.
Description: Elves are the magic users of the game. They are excellent spell casters and have decent resistance to elemental magic. They are not, however, very good at fighting with weapons and have low constitution, making them more susceptible to physical damage.

Virtue Effect: You recover steadily, increasing healing received.
Sin Effect: Envy undermines resolve, slightly reducing your critical damage spikes.
Description: Half elves are the result of the interbreeding between humans and elves. They are almost as versatile as humans and possess an improved magical prowess, as well as mild elemental resistance. Like their elf cousins, they do have a slight susceptibility to physical damage.

Virtue Effect: Your charge cannot be broken by pain alone; only incapacitation can interrupt it.
Sin Effect: You advance slowly, gaining reduced experience from combat.
Description: We do not speculate on how they are made but we do know the union between humans and giants does occur. These half giants dwarf most men but are seen as runts amongst their giant brethren. Their brutish nature make the excellent Warriors and not much else. Half giants have mild resistances to poisons and physical damage but poor agility and sharp weaknesses against most other magics, especially holy spells.

Virtue Effect: Your charm opens purses; charisma has a stronger effect on gold outcomes.
Sin Effect: When you carry too much, the penalties of encumbrance are harsher.
Description: Gnomes are very charismatic, giving them a distinct advantage in money making, vendor relations, and are especially lucky. They are also above average spell caster with a slight affinity toward the divine, giving them a slight resistance to holy spells. Gnomes prefer the civilized world and thus are not found among the ranks of Pathfinders.

Virtue Effect: Combat consumables are more effective (does not affect permanent stat potions).
Sin Effect: Overindulgence brings a hangover: using combat consumables can hinder your next fight.
Description: Dwarves are short in stature only, being amongst the strongest both in body and will. They are lacking in physical agility and have a healthy mistrust of the arcane. As beings of the Earth, dwarves have resistance against earth, poison, and physical damage but are weak against shadow magic.

Virtue Effect: You endure the worst blows, taking reduced damage from critical hits.
Sin Effect: Pain can trigger Blind Rage: you keep control, but your aim suffers briefly.
Description: Half orcs are the result of interbreeding between humans and orcs, which while rare does occur. While not a strong as their fullblood brethren, half orcs are much stronger on average than humans. However the stigma related to half orcs makes them far less charismatic, while there inherit bloodlust makes any pursuit of the divine unappealing.
